recent_posts.title: Semaphore v1.4 Release
recent_posts.summary: Semaphore v1.4 introduces partial pipeline rebuilds, allowing developers to rerun only failed parts of a pipeline instead of the entire workflow, saving CI minutes and debugging time. The release also adds the ability to skip CI builds for draft pull requests, reducing unnecessary resource usage. Additional improvements include enhanced HTML tag support in markdown reports, API workflow parameters for dynamic pipeline behavior, extended session timeouts up to 30 days, and various performance optimizations.

recent_posts.title: GPT-OSS: Specs, Setup, and Self-Hosting Guide
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI released GPT-OSS-20B and GPT-OSS-120B, their first open-source large language models under Apache 2.0 license. The 20B model runs on consumer hardware with 16-32GB RAM, while the 120B model requires data center GPUs. Both feature chain-of-thought reasoning, configurable effort levels, fine-tuning support, and 128k token context windows. Users can test them via OpenAI's playground, HuggingFace, or API providers, and run them locally using LM Studio, Ollama, or vLLM. Cloud hosting costs range from $4,000-$12,000 monthly for dedicated GPU instances, with shared options available for lower costs.

recent_posts.title: Cloud vs Hybrid: A Guide to Choosing Semaphore Editions
recent_posts.summary: Compares Semaphore Cloud versus Hybrid CI/CD solutions, providing a decision framework based on compliance requirements, cost analysis, and hidden expenses. Explains when self-hosting makes sense versus using fully managed services, including setup costs, maintenance burden, and productivity impacts that can outweigh infrastructure savings.

recent_posts.title: Sara Vieira on Game Boys, JavaScript, and Community
recent_posts.summary: Sara Vieira shares her journey from customizing Hi5 profiles to becoming a JavaScript developer and conference speaker. She discusses her current passion for hardware projects including Game Boy refurbishment, 3D printing, and building emulators. Sara emphasizes the value of small, passionate communities over corporate-driven tech spaces and offers practical advice for aspiring conference speakers to start with meetups and lightning talks.

recent_posts.title: Semaphore vs BitBucket Pipelines
recent_posts.summary: Semaphore Community Edition offers open-source flexibility with Apache 2.0 licensing, self-hosting capabilities, and support for multiple Git providers, while Bitbucket Pipelines provides tight Atlassian ecosystem integration but is limited to cloud-only deployment. Semaphore features a visual pipeline editor, real-time feedback, and built-in test dashboards, whereas Bitbucket relies on YAML configuration and has limited free tier minutes. For teams prioritizing control and portability, Semaphore CE provides better value, while Bitbucket suits organizations already invested in Atlassian tools.

recent_posts.title: Semaphore vs Travis CI
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive comparison between Semaphore CE and Travis CI covering licensing models, pipeline setup approaches, Git platform support, monorepo capabilities, test reporting features, and installation complexity. Semaphore CE offers open-source licensing under Apache 2.0, visual pipeline editor, native monorepo support, and simpler installation, while Travis CI provides proprietary closed-source platform with strong build matrix support but lacks modern workflow features like native monorepo handling.

recent_posts.title: GitHub Actions vs Semaphore
recent_posts.summary: GitHub Actions offers tight GitHub integration and convenience but creates vendor lock-in with its closed-source, proprietary nature. Semaphore Community Edition provides an open-source alternative with Apache-2 licensing, supporting multiple Git providers, visual pipeline editing, built-in test reports, and easier monorepo handling. While GitHub Actions requires third-party solutions for advanced features like test dashboards, Semaphore CE includes these capabilities natively. The choice depends on whether teams prioritize GitHub ecosystem integration or prefer open-source flexibility with platform-agnostic CI/CD capabilities.

recent_posts.title: Gou Rao on Agentic Systems in DevOps
recent_posts.summary: Gou Rao, co-founder of Neubird, discusses how their AI-powered tool Hawkeye transforms DevOps incident response by using LLMs to reason across telemetry data rather than just generate responses. Unlike traditional AI assistants, Hawkeye acts as a digital engineer that investigates logs, metrics, and traces to diagnose issues and suggest remediation steps. The system prioritizes accuracy over speed, taking minutes to provide well-reasoned analysis while showing its chain of thought for transparency. Currently focused on recommendations rather than autonomous actions, Hawkeye helps teams from startups to enterprises reduce time spent on alert triage and root cause analysis.

recent_posts.title: Semaphore v1.3 Release Roundup: A Big Leap for Contributors and Small Teams 🚀
recent_posts.summary: Semaphore v1.3 introduces major improvements for open source contributors including automatic CI for forked PRs, public access to pipeline jobs, and local development support with Skaffold requiring 7GB RAM and 5 CPUs. The release also launches a free Enterprise Edition for small teams (under 50 employees, less than $5M ARR) with advanced RBAC and compliance features. Additional enhancements include better workflow navigation with stateful pagination and date-based filtering, plus upcoming bug bounty program via Algora.

recent_posts.title: How Semaphore built Plumber using Elixir and finite state machines for CI/CD orchestration
recent_posts.summary: Semaphore's Plumber engine orchestrates CI/CD pipelines using a finite state machine architecture built in Elixir. The system manages pipeline execution through distinct states (initializing, pending, running, done) with dedicated Looper processes handling each state. Key components include PostgreSQL for transactional integrity, RabbitMQ for service communication, and Kubernetes for deployment. The architecture provides fault tolerance through supervision trees, recovery mechanisms for stuck pipelines, and horizontal scalability across distributed agents.
